But what exactly is “the cloud”? It’s a term we hear constantly, yet it can feel abstract and complex.This guide breaks down the essentials. We’ll explore what the cloud is, why it’s a game-changer, and how it works.What is Cloud Computing?At its core, the cloud isn’t a physical place; it’s a global network of servers. Cloud computing is the practice of using the internet to access IT resources like storage, processing power, or software instead of hosting them on your own devices. It’s about storing and accessing your data on remote servers.The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) defines cloud computing by five essential characteristics:On-Demand Self-Service: You can get computing resources whenever you need them, on your ownBroad Network Access: You can access these resources over the internet from anywhereResource Pooling: The cloud provider allocates resources to many users from a shared poolCreate an account to read the full story.The author made this story available to Medium members only.If you’re new to Medium, create a new account to read this story on us.Continue in appOr, continue in mobile webSign up with GoogleSign up with FacebookSign up with emailAlready have an account?
